newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Feb borrowing need seen -10 bln SKR. [CORRECTED 10:37 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Swedish Feb borrowing need seen -10 bln SKR. [CORRECTED 10:37 GMT]

text.p: Sweden's state borrowing requirement for February 1997 was forecast at minus 10 billion crowns, the National Debt Office said on Thursday.
The office left its forecast for the 1997 borrowing requirement at 20 to 30 billion crowns. This was lowered in December from a previous forecast range of 25 to 35 billion crowns.
"A borrowing requirement of -9.8 billion crowns is foreseen for February, which is 24.3-billion crowns higher than in February 1996," the National Debt Office said in a statement.
It said the higher borrowing requirement this year was largely due to changes made to the payment and accounting periods for value added tax in January 1996.
"These changes led to higher value added tax revenues every second month and lower revenues in the intervening months.
"They also gave rise to an additional collection of value added tax in February 1996," the office said.
The office said a new five-year bond paying 5.5-percent coupon interest would be introduced in February.

"In connection with the bond issue on February 12, 1997, the debt office intends to introduce a new five-year government bond, Loan 1039, maturing on April 12, 2002, which will pay coupon interest of 5.5 percent," the office said.
It said the new bond would have benchmark status, which means the debt office's dealers would be expected to quote two-way prices for the loan.
"As with the latest issues of new loans, the Swedish National Debt Office will ensure adequate liquidity on the market for Loan 1039 by providing a repo facility," it said.

The facility would cover a total outstanding volume of 15 billion crowns, including the issued amount, meaning the debt office can offer repos for the difference between 15 billion crowns and the amount issued by that time.
The office would invite investors to make exchanges in order to improve the liquidity of the new loan.
"Investors will be invited to sell Loan 1028, which matures in January 1999, and buy loan 1039 for the same nominal amount instead," the office said.
This would facilitate the refinancing of Loan 1028, it said.

For investors who do not want to increase the interest sensitivity of their portfolios, the debt office will also provide a facility to exchange a combination of Loan 1028 and Loan 1035 (maturing in 2005) for the new five-year loan.
These offers would apply to a maximum aggregate volume of 20 billion crowns of the new five-year bond.

The borrowing requirement for 1996 totalled 21 billion crowns, a fall of 117.5 billion from 1995 and 4.6 billion crowns lower (corrects from higher) than the final forecast last month. The primary balance improved by 49.6 billion crowns.
"This improvement was mainly due to higher revenues in the form of income tax, value added tax and excise duties," the debt office said.
Lower spending by the Labour Market Board, defence services and the Immigration Board also helped.
The borrowing requirement for January, which the office raised to 2.4 billion crowns from a forecast of zero one month ago, was mostly because of European Union payments.
"The increase in the borrowing requirement is largely due to the reperiodisation of payments to the EU and will not affect the borrowing requirement for 1997 as a whole," it said.
-- Abigail Schmelz, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1003
